title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 115
paragraphs: As the army marched on from the Strymon, it found a shore running toward the setting sun, and it passed by the Greek city of Argilus, which is situated there. This region, and the country lying above it, is called Bisaltia. Then, keeping on his left the gulf off Posideion, he went through the plain called the plain of Syleus, passing the Greek city of Stageirus, and so came to Acanthus, taking along with him as he went every one of these tribes and of those who dwell around Pangaeum, just as he had done with those I listed before — those by the coast serving in the fleet, those inland accompanying him on foot. This road along which Xerxes the king led his army, the Thracians neither disturb nor sow over, but hold it in the greatest reverence to this day.
